Original questions, instructions and judgment labels authored for this Research workflow; MIT license.

domains.title: Reported result and source basis
domains.description: Establish which result is being appraised and whether its stated measure, population, timing and precision can be traced through the retained reports.

fields.label: Describe the exact outcome, measure, timepoint, analysis population and comparison represented by this saved result.
fields.help: Use the original result and report selectors. Distinguish group totals from category or analysis denominators; retain reported missing or non-estimable precision.

fields.label: Describe what can be reconstructed from the retained reports and what information the source leaves unresolved.
fields.help: Identify the relevant source locations. Use not_reported or unavailable when the underlying information is absent; explain how that affects this appraisal.

domains.title: Formation of the comparison
domains.description: Examine the source-described process that produced the compared groups, records or samples, with attention to factors that could change the result.

fields.label: Describe how the compared groups or sample were formed and which source details establish the design.
fields.help: Use the design selected for this assessment. Address allocation, recruitment or sample selection as applicable to this result.

fields.label: Explain which reported features of group formation or baseline differences could influence this particular comparison.
fields.help: Separate a reported feature from its proposed effect. When the source does not permit a judgment, record that information gap explicitly.

domains.title: Exposure, care and follow-up
domains.description: Examine how exposure, intervention delivery, subsequent care and follow-up relate to the result being interpreted.

fields.label: Describe the source-reported exposure or intervention, subsequent care and follow-up relevant to this result.
fields.help: Explain which details matter for the chosen outcome and timepoint. Mark a field not_applicable only with an assessment-specific rationale.

fields.label: Explain whether reported departures, crossovers, differential care or incomplete follow-up could affect the comparison.
fields.help: Preserve the report's stated facts and the reviewer's reasoning separately. Do not convert missing descriptions into an assertion that no departures occurred.

domains.title: Measurement and available observations
domains.description: Examine how the outcome was measured and how the available records correspond to the target analysis.

fields.label: Describe the outcome measurement, timing, assessor or data source, and any reported differences between groups.
fields.help: Tie the answer to the selected outcome and its original report locations; document any relevant measurement limitations.

fields.label: Describe the reported available, excluded or missing observations and their possible implications for this result.
fields.help: Use the result-specific denominators. Retain unknown counts as unknown, and distinguish an observed source count from an inferred mechanism.

domains.title: Analysis and choice of reported result
domains.description: Examine the stated analysis, available prespecified context and the choice of the reported result.

fields.label: Describe the analysis and any available prespecified outcome, timepoint or method that can be linked to this result.
fields.help: Retain the actual reported statistic, adjustment and precision. A registry or protocol can be linked as a separate original occurrence when available.

fields.label: Explain whether the available records leave a material concern about the analysis or choice of this reported result.
fields.help: State the specific source basis and uncertainty. Distinguish an unresolved question from an established reporting discrepancy.

judgments.label: No material concern identified
judgments.description: The reviewer explains why the available source supports this judgment for the selected domain or overall result.

judgments.label: Concern affects interpretation
judgments.description: The reviewer identifies a source-backed concern and explains its likely relevance to the result.

judgments.label: Material concern
judgments.description: The reviewer identifies a substantial source-backed limitation that changes confidence in the result.

judgments.label: Insufficient information
judgments.description: The available reports do not support a resolved judgment; the reviewer records what is missing and why it matters.

judgments.label: Not applicable
judgments.description: The reviewer explains why the selected domain does not apply to this design and result.
